article_title: E3Sense: Head-Confined Multimodal Sensing of Learner Engagement
citation: Sidharth Anupkrishnan, Itir Sayar, Jeongah Lee, Sri Harsha Musunuri, Guan-Ming Su, Madeline Endres, Ravi Karkar, Phuc Nguyen. (2026). E3Sense: Head-Confined Multimodal Sensing of Learner Engagement. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26569
title: E3Sense: a head-worn multimodal engagement-sensing platform co-locating dry-electrode EEG, eye-tracking glasses, and forehead EDA
description: E3Sense is a sensing platform that "co-locates three devices on the head": a four-channel dry-electrode EEG headband, Pupil Labs Neon eye-tracking glasses, and an EmotiBit EDA sensor with two dry forehead electrodes spaced by the eye-tracker frame. Software aligns the three independently clocked streams on device-native timestamps and computes a fixed 166-dimensional per-segment feature vector (28 EEG, 127 eye-tracking, 11 EDA features) from a 120 s analysis window, fed to classical model families for engagement prediction.
requirements: All sensing sites lie on the head, and the EEG and EDA electrodes are dry, enabling faster gel-free setup
Stream alignment on device-native timestamps and periodic clock anchors so features from one window trace to the same viewing stretch
constraints: The present configuration uses three devices, and its predictive performance does not establish comfort or ease of everyday use
Forehead EDA is characterized as relatively resistant to motion artifacts but less responsive than palmar recordings, motivating a feasibility evaluation rather than an equivalence claim
target_learners: adult university-campus participants watching educational videos
target_learning_goals: segment-level self-reported engagement during video learning, to inform engagement-aware adaptive interfaces
examples: In the lab study, 30 participants watched three of four educational videos in a 2×2 content/format design under continuous sensing, rating five segments per video, yielding 450 segment-level observations
